title: 1958 London County Council election
summary: Labour won its largest-ever landslide at County Hall, taking 101 of the 126 elected seats on 58.4% of the vote — eight in every ten councillors. The Conservatives were reduced to 25 seats as Labour's dominance of London government reached its peak.
highlights: Labour's biggest LCC landslide: 101 of 126 seats
Labour wins 58.4% of the vote, its highest LCC share
Eight in ten councillors are now Labour

council.note: 126 directly elected councillors, plus aldermen chosen by the council. Seat shares are taken from Rallings & Thrasher's record of LCC results.

sources.label: Rallings & Thrasher, London County Council Elections 1889–1961 (Elections Centre)
